general_conventions: M1 = method mark; a later A1 that depends on it cannot be scored without it; in 'show that' items the final A mark is often A0 (the given value earns nothing on its own).
C1 = compensatory method mark, awarded automatically if the final answer is correct; A1 = accuracy mark for the final value; B1 = independent mark for a stated fact or step.

ECF (error carried forward): later numerical parts can earn full credit if consistent with an earlier wrong answer; ECF is allowed after arithmetic (AE), transcription (TE) and power-of-ten (POT) errors but not after wrong physics / wrong equation (XP).
POT: power-of-ten slip (usually an SI-prefix conversion) loses the mark where it occurs, then ECF applies.

SF: giving more significant figures than justified is not penalised; too few is dealt with in individual guidance (often 1 SF is allowed where stated); the SF penalty is applied only once in the paper unless a question explicitly demands a given number of SF.
XP: use of an incorrect equation counts as wrong physics even if it happens to give the right number.
CON: a contradiction within the same response cancels the mark; BOD = benefit of doubt; ^ marks an omission (not wrong but incomplete).

Notation: '/' separates alternatives; Reject/Not = not creditworthy; Ignore = irrelevant extra; Allow = acceptable; words in brackets are not essential; underlined words must be present; AW = alternative wording; ORA = or reverse argument.
General rule for Section B: substitution into an equation may be made with any quantity as subject unless the guidance says otherwise.
Level-of-response annotations L1/L2/L3 exist in the generic list (L1 = 2/1 marks, L2 = 4/3, L3 = 6/5) but this paper has no LoR question.
Section A MCQ: 1 mark each for the correct letter only.
Anomaly: the MS total row for Q26 says 8, but the item marks (2+2+3) sum to 7, consistent with a 70-mark paper.

questions.context: Choose the missing word in a statement of Archimedes' principle.

pitfalls: An LDR is a passive resistive component; it converts no energy into electrical energy.

pitfalls: Forgetting to convert 30 g to kg or omitting g.

questions.context: Choose which resistor arrangement on the same supply dissipates least power.
pitfalls: Least power corresponds to the largest total resistance, not the smallest.

New de Broglie wavelength when proton KE is doubled.

Region of EM spectrum for a 2.5 eV photon.

questions.topic: 3.5 Newton's laws of motion and momentum
questions.context: Which graph's area gives impulse.
Deduce from a dripping tap diagram that droplets accelerate.
questions.answer: Gaps between successive drops increase further down.
marking_points: B1: separation of droplets increases with distance fallen (equal time intervals)
pitfalls: Just saying 'gravity acts' without referring to the evidence in the diagram.

questions.topic: 3.5 Newton's laws of motion and momentum
questions.context: Explain using a Newton law why a trolley stays still relative to ground when truck accelerates.
questions.answer: No (negligible) resultant force acts on trolley so it stays at rest (N1, or F = ma with F = 0).
marking_points: B1: no motion explained via first law (stays at rest unless a resultant force acts) or second law (F = 0 so a = 0)
B1: there is no/negligible resultant force on the trolley
allow_reject_ignore: Allow no frictional/extra/new force for the second point.
pitfalls: Quoting the third law; not stating that the resultant force is zero.

questions.context: Use a displacement–time graph for uniform acceleration to show speed at 4.0 s is 10 m/s.
questions.answer: 10 m s^-1 (tangent gradient 9.5–10.5, or s = 20 m with s = ½at^2 then v = at)
marking_points: C1: tangent drawn at t = 4.0 s
A1: gradient gives v in range 9.50–10.50 m/s
Alternative: C1 s = 20 m with s = ½at^2; C1 a = 2.5 m/s^2; C1 v = at or v^2 = 2as (working essential); A0 for 10
allow_reject_ignore: Other correct methods allowed.
pitfalls: Using s/t (average speed, 5 m/s) instead of a tangent.
Show-that: the final 10 is worth nothing — working must be visible.

questions.topic: 3.5 Newton's laws of motion and momentum
questions.context: Rate of change of momentum of a 1200 kg car over first 4.0 s, with unit.
marking_points: C1: change in momentum = 1200 × 10 = 12000 kg m/s (or F = 1200 × 2.5)
B1: unit kg m s^-2 or N
allow_reject_ignore: ECF from (c)(i).
Allow 'newton'.
pitfalls: Giving momentum (12000) instead of rate of change; unit kg m s^-1 instead of N.

questions.topic: 1.1 Practical skills assessed in a written examination
questions.context: Name instrument for measuring a height of 0.100 ± 0.002 m.
questions.answer: Metre rule / ruler with mm scale
marking_points: B1: ruler with mm scale (any mm-scale instrument e.g. tape)
allow_reject_ignore: NOT callipers or micrometer.
pitfalls: Choosing callipers/micrometer — wrong range for 10 cm with ±2 mm.

questions.context: Absolute uncertainty in g = v^2/2d given d and v with uncertainties, to 2 SF.
marking_points: C1: correct fractional/percentage uncertainties of d and v, or g = 1.4^2/(2×0.100) evaluated
Alternative: C1 gmax 11.48 or gmin 8.28; C1 range 3.2; A1 1.6
allow_reject_ignore: Allow 1 SF for intermediate uncertainties.
Not just g = 9.8 for first C1 — working must be seen.
Ignore value of g on answer line (e.g. 9.8 ± 1.6).
pitfalls: Forgetting to double the % uncertainty in v because it is squared.
Not giving answer to 2 SF (required).

questions.context: With a circuit diagram, describe determining an LED's threshold voltage accurately in a bright lab.
questions.answer: Circuit with LED, voltmeter, ammeter, variable supply; increase p.d. until LED just lights/current starts; shield LED with tube or dim lights.
marking_points: B1: correct circuit — LED (right polarity), voltmeter across, ammeter, means of varying p.d.
B1: increase p.d. until LED just lights / current just registers (ORA)
B1: use a tube over LED or switch lights off to see onset of light
allow_reject_ignore: Allow variable supply or variable resistor.
Shielding tube may be shown on labelled diagram.
pitfalls: LED drawn in reverse bias; no method of varying p.d.; ignoring the brightly-lit condition.

questions.subtopic: current as rate of flow of charge
questions.context: Number of electrons per second for a current of 0.045 A.
Mean drift velocity in a 0.24 mm diameter filament with given n and current.
allow_reject_ignore: 2 marks for 2.5×10^-5 (using 0.24 mm as radius — POT/diameter slip).
pitfalls: Using diameter as radius; mm to m conversion.

questions.context: Explain why p.d. across a thermistor in series with a resistor falls after switch-on.
questions.answer: Current heats thermistor, its resistance falls, so its share of p.d. falls.
marking_points: B1: current causes thermistor temperature to rise
B1: thermistor resistance decreases (or current rises so resistor p.d. rises) so V falls
allow_reject_ignore: Allow warms/heats up.
Ignore 'temperature of circuit increases'.
pitfalls: Saying the whole circuit heats rather than the thermistor.

questions.context: Use the V–t graph to find thermistor resistance at time T.
marking_points: C1: read V = 2.4 V (or resistor p.d. 3.6 V)
C1: I = 0.30 A (or potential divider equation 2.4 = R/(R+12) × 6.0)
allow_reject_ignore: Not V = 2.2 V (misread) but ECF allowed from it.
Allow 8 (1 SF).
pitfalls: Misreading the graph scale (2.2 V instead of 2.4 V).

questions.context: State why X-rays and UV from the same event arrive together.
questions.answer: All EM waves travel at the same speed c in vacuum (3.0 × 10^8 m/s).
marking_points: B1: both travel at same speed / speed of light / 3.0×10^8 m/s
allow_reject_ignore: Ignore just 'travels at c'.

questions.context: Frequency of X-rays of wavelength 2.5 × 10^-11 m.
Estimate number of ~500 nm photons produced from one X-ray photon's energy.
marking_points: C1: use of E = hf or E = hc/λ
C1: ratio of wavelengths, energies (7.96×10^-15 / 3.98×10^-19) or frequencies
allow_reject_ignore: ECF from (b).
pitfalls: Inverting the ratio.

questions.context: State why sound cannot be polarised.
Describe and explain a lab demonstration of sound diffraction.
questions.answer: Loudspeaker, gap/slit, microphone; sound detected spreading beyond gap; gap width comparable to wavelength.
marking_points: B1: loudspeaker, microphone (or ear) and slit/gap
B1: sound spreads out after passing through gap (AW)
B1: gap size comparable to wavelength of sound
allow_reject_ignore: Allow doorway for gap, receiver for microphone.
Not 'diffraction' as the spreading statement — it is in the stem.
pitfalls: Just restating 'it diffracts' without describing spreading.

questions.context: Define refractive index of a material.
questions.answer: n = speed of light in vacuum ÷ speed of light in the material
marking_points: B1: speed of light in vacuum / speed of light in material
allow_reject_ignore: Allow n = c/v if all terms defined.
NOT speed of light in air for c.
Light must be mentioned at least once.
pitfalls: Saying 'air' instead of vacuum; quoting Snell's law instead.

questions.context: Compare wavelength in B (higher n) with wavelength in A.
questions.answer: Frequency unchanged, light slower in B, so λB < λA (λB ≈ 0.77λA).
marking_points: B1: frequency same in A and B
B1: light slower in B (vB = 0.77vA) ORA
B1: v = fλ so λB < λA
allow_reject_ignore: Allow v directly proportional to λ.
pitfalls: Not stating frequency is constant.

questions.context: Angle of refraction in B when incidence angle in A is 60°, nB = 1.3nA.
Whether TIR occurs for light going from A to B at any angle.
questions.answer: No — TIR only when light travels into a lower refractive index (B to A).
marking_points: B1: TIR/critical angle only possible for light going from B to A (to lower n) AW
allow_reject_ignore: Not θ < φ alone.

questions.context: Show from moments that y = (F/ALρg)x for a suspended rod with attached object.
questions.answer: Rod weight ALρg × y = F × x, rearranged.
allow_reject_ignore: Allow W or mg.
pitfalls: Not expressing weight via density and volume.

questions.context: Draw best-fit line through y–x data and find gradient.
pitfalls: Using a small triangle or data points not on line.

questions.context: Use gradient with F, L, A to find density of the rod metal.
allow_reject_ignore: ECF from (b)(i); answer must match candidate's gradient.
Allow 1 SF (8 × 10^3).
pitfalls: Rearranging wrongly so ρ appears in numerator.
